# TDPdf v1.22.0.0

**There are no changes to the application in this release.** No fix, no feature, no difference in behaviour from v1.21.0.0 — if you are already running 1.21.0.0, you are running the same editor and do not need to upgrade.

What changed is how TDPdf is built and delivered. This is the first release produced end to end by the automated pipeline rather than by hand, and it is versioned so that build is identifiable.

## What's actually new

### The build is signed, reproducible from a tag, and complete
Pushing a version tag now produces the whole release on its own: it compiles, signs the executable, publishes it here, and updates the managed deployment. Previously signing and deployment were manual steps performed on a separate Windows machine.

The download is now **signed**, and this release also carries two things earlier releases should have included and did not:

- `TDPdf-1.22.0.0-src.zip` — the GPLv3 corresponding source for exactly this build
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — checksums, so you can verify what you downloaded

### Two long-standing build faults, fixed
Both failed silently, which is why they lasted:

- The **corresponding-source archive was never actually produced** by any tagged release. The step that builds it invoked a Windows-only shell on a Linux build machine and ignored its own failure. The source has always been available in the public repository, so the licence was satisfied throughout — but the archive that is supposed to accompany each release was simply missing. It is attached from now on.
- The **optional telemetry key was never embedded** by automated builds. The generator wrote its output to a path containing a Windows-style separator, which on Linux produced a file with a backslash in its name that the project never read. Automated builds therefore shipped the inert placeholder. Since telemetry is opt-in and off by default, this changed nothing for anyone in practice.

## For administrators

If you deploy TDPdf through Intune, the detection rule now requires 1.22.0.0, so managed machines will reinstall despite the application being unchanged. That is expected. Deployment assignments are unaffected.

## Verifying this download

The executable is signed by *The Doodle Project Code Signing*, a private certificate. On managed machines that trust it, the signature validates. On a machine that does not, Windows will still warn on first run — a self-signed certificate is not a public trust anchor, and this release does not change that. Use `SHA256SUMS.txt` if you want to confirm the download independently.

If you hit something, please [open an issue](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/issues).
